hints: Focus on what alkaline iodine is really testing for, the yellow precipitate of triiodomethane means the iodoform reaction.
Recall that only ethanal and methyl ketones containing the $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$ group give a positive result, so start listing all seven carbonyls with 4 or fewer carbons.
Count how many of your listed aldehydes and ketones actually contain a $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}$ unit attached to H or to another carbon.
walkthrough:
**Recall the iodoform test**

Yellow precipitate with alkaline $\text{I}_2(\text{aq})$ is $\text{CHI}_3$, triiodomethane. It forms only from a very specific group.

Test rule:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CO}- \text{ group gives CHI}_3 \text{ precipitate}$$

**List all seven carbonyl compounds**

We need every aldehyde and ketone with one O and 1 to 4 carbons. Let's count them systematically.

Aldehydes (5): $\text{HCHO}$, $\text{CH}_3\text{CHO}$, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CHO}$, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CHO}$, $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CHCHO}$

Ketones (2): $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3$, $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_2\text{CH}_3$

**Pick out the positive ones**

Now check for the $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$ unit. Ethanal is $\text{CH}_3\text{CHO}$, which behaves like this group.

Positive: $\text{CH}_3\text{CHO}$ (ethanal), $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3$ (propanone), $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_2\text{CH}_3$ (butan-2-one).

That is 3 compounds in total, so the count is 3.

options.A: 1 is too low. It would mean you counted only one methyl ketone, perhaps propanone, and missed that ethanal and butan-2-one also contain the $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}$ unit.
options.B: 2 is too low. A common slip is to count the two methyl ketones (propanone and butanone) but forget that ethanal, $\text{CH}_3\text{CHO}$, also gives a positive iodoform test.
options.C: 3 is correct. Of the seven compounds, exactly three contain the required group: ethanal, propanone and butan-2-one. All three form yellow $\text{CHI}_3$ with alkaline $\text{I}_2$.
options.D: 4 is too high. You may have incorrectly included propanal or butanal. Only a methyl group directly attached to the carbonyl carbon works, so $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CHO}$ does not give the test.
